items.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I knew about it, of course. ... The interesting thing about Leonard was, he was born in England... he was one of the first people in the United States to make a considerable impact...

ctx.x: He was a writer by trade. He made a living writing.

I assume he did. He was involved in a number of books. He did liner notes and the like. You see, in those days, though, I don’t know that anybody made a full-time living out of writing about jazz. Ralph Gleason in San Francisco did to a certain extent, but he wrote about the whole cultural music scene, etc. Leonard Feather probably came closest to a writer who made a living out of writing about jazz.
Were you aware of Roger Pryor Dodge at that time? Or was that someone . . .?
